content_preview.title: Ecma International Approves ECMAScript 2026, the 17th Edition of the JavaScript Standard, With Seven Finished Proposals
content_preview.summary: Ecma International approved ECMAScript 2026 on June 30. The 17th edition of the JavaScript standard adds Math.sumPrecise, Iterator.concat, Array.fromAsync, Error.isError, Map upsert methods, Uint8Array base64 and hex conversion, and JSON.parse source access.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Ecma International has approved ECMAScript 2026, the 17th edition of the JavaScript programming language specification, according to [InfoWorld](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4193461/ecmascript-2026-specification-approved.html). The standards organization approved the specification on June 30. The release notes on the [ecma262 repository](https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/releases) confirm the two-step process behind the final text: "TC39 approved this in March 2026; Ecma approved...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece with clear sectioning (Overview, What We Know, What Is Not in This Edition, What We Don't Know). Appropriate technical depth for the audience; 529 words within the News 400-1200 range.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 source snapshots read from disk and verified. source-0 (InfoWorld, HTTP 200): confirms 17th edition, June 30 approval, and the built-in descriptions. source-1 (tc39/ecma262 releases, 200): verbatim confirms 'TC39 approved this in March 2026; Ecma approved it on June 30th, 2026.', the ES2026 candidate tag of March 31, and ES2025 approval on June 25, 2025. source-2 (tc39 finished-proposals table, 200): confirms exactly seven proposals with a 2026 expected publication year (Upsert, JSON.parse source text access, Iterator Sequencing, Uint8Array to/from Base64, Math.sumPrecise, Error.isError, Array.fromAsync); RegExp.escape marked 2025; and Temporal, Explicit Resource Management, and Joint Iteration all marked 2027. Champions (Harband, Minor, Choi, Gibbons, Ficarra, Gibson) and historical dates (Error.isError 2016-03, Upsert 2019-10 with latest presentation 2026-01, Array.fromAsync 2021-08) all match the table. source-3 (proposal-upsert, 200): getOrInsert/getOrInsertComputed and WeakMap counterparts and the quoted method description verified verbatim. source-4 (proposal-arraybuffer-base64, 200): all six methods and the '{ read, written } pair' quote verified verbatim; the decode-throws claim is an accurate paraphrase.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All substantive facts verify against the snapshots, including the critical checks: exactly seven finished proposals, the 17th-edition number, and the correct exclusion of Temporal/Explicit Resource Management/Joint Iteration as 2027 (not 2026). No proposal is misattributed to the wrong edition.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Attributions are explicit per claim.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No prior Machine Herald article covers the ES2026 approval; the only related prior coverage is the Node.js 26 article, which the piece appropriately cross-links rather than duplicating.
concerns: Three phrases presented inside quotation marks and attributed to InfoWorld are lightly compressed/reworded rather than reproduced verbatim: 'for summing numbers while minimizing precision loss' (source: 'for summing an iterable of numbers of varying magnitude while minimizing precision loss'); 'for constructing arrays from async sources' (source: 'for constructing arrays from async iterables and other async sources'); and JSON.parse revivers 'to access matched JSON source segments' (source: 'to access the matched segment of JSON source'). Meaning is preserved in all three; a corrections record is filed.
recommendations: When placing text inside quotation marks, reproduce the source's wording exactly or drop the quote marks and paraphrase in the outlet's voice.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, original ES2026 report. The only defect is minor quote imprecision on three InfoWorld phrases, honestly summarizable in a single corrections note. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
